Buyers flock to Dangwa Flower Market in Manila on Mother’s Day, driving heavy foot traffic and a surge in demand for blooms.

Vendors said prices of various flower varieties have increased as families and loved ones purchase bouquets and arrangements for the annual celebration honoring mothers and motherhood.

FROM PALESTINE TO THE PHILIPPINES, WE WILL BE FREE!

A free screening of animations and documentaries exploring food, conflict, and resistance from Palestine to the Philippines will be held at the UP Film Institute on May 18 at 2:00 PM.

Co-presented with the Philippine-Palestine Friendship Association and Mowelfund Film Institute, Food & Fire: Ecologies of War from Palestine to the Philippines examines how food becomes both a site of survival and struggle amid conflict and displacement.

The full lineup of films is as follows:

Animation
· 'The Last Fish in the World' by Tina Basco and Patricia Sim
· 'Flush' by Roland Cartagena
· 'Pastil: Parehas re ta'g Kan-on'g Ginakaon' by Andrei Francis C. Arrocena

Documentary
· 'Samiah Domado Monir, Food for Peace' by Babai Women’s Network
· 'Manang' by Eizen James Alilam, Kaycel Galvez, Victor Morillo Macam III, Larz Maurice Salas, and Leaux Tecson Ambrocio
· 'Everyday Nakba' by Mohammad Al-Azza
· 'Foragers' by Jumana Manna

The screening will be followed by a discussion with food historian Ige Ramos, Gail Orduña of the People's Coalition on Food Sovereignty, and Fatma Cargolio of the Philippine-Palestine Friendship Association, moderated by Menchani Tilendo.

Visit the UPFI Facebook page for more details.
